name: Question 20
problem:
The values of functions $h(x)$ and $z(x)$ and their derivatives at $t=2$ are given in the table below.

| $t$ | $h(t)$ | $z(t)$ | ${h}^{′}(t)$ | ${z}^{′}(t)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $5$ | $8$ | $-3$ | $4$ |

If $f(t)=\frac{1-h(t)}{z(t)},$ compute ${f}^{′}(2).$
worked_solution:
The quotient rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{u}{v})=\frac{{u}^{′}v-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}}.
$$

Let $u=1-h(t)$ and $v=z(t).$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=-{h}^{′}(t)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={z}^{′}(t).
$$

Substituting this into the quotient rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{{u}^{′}v-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-{h}^{′}(t))\cdot z(t)-(1-h(t))\cdot {z}^{′}(t)}{(z(t))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-z(t){h}^{′}(t)-{z}^{′}(t)(1-h(t))}{{z}^{2}(t)}.\end{aligned}
$$

At $t=2,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(2) & =\frac{-z(2){h}^{′}(2)-{z}^{′}(2)(1-h(2))}{{z}^{2}(2)} \\  & =\frac{-8\cdot (-3)-4\cdot (1-5)}{{8}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{24+16}{64} \\  & =\frac{5}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

The values of functions h(x) and z(x) and their derivatives at t=2 are given in the table below.

t h(t) z(t) h′(t) z′(t)
2 5 8 −3 4

If f(t)=1−h(t)z(t), compute f′(2).

a
53
b
−38
c
58
d
25
e
54
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The quotient rule states that ddt(uv)=u′v−uv′v2.

Let u=1−h(t) and v=z(t). Differentiating each, we get dudt=−h′(t)anddvdt=z′(t).

Substituting this into the quotient rule gives f′(t)=u′v−uv′v2=(−h′(t))⋅z(t)−(1−h(t))⋅z′(t)(z(t))2=−z(t)h′(t)−z′(t)(1−h(t))z2(t).

At t=2, this gives

f′(2)=−z(2)h′(2)−z′(2)(1−h(2))z2(2)=−8⋅(−3)−4⋅(1−5)82=24+1664=58.
